concerns.text: The plan's own analysis states the only verified dataset 'does not contain improvisation-task labels, expert improvisation ratings, years-of-training, or the covariate metadata'. The dependent variable (improvisation skill) therefore has no construct instantiation in any obtainable data, so the planned design cannot answer the research question the spec poses. The conditional halt path is honest, but a plan whose primary analysis is expected to halt is not a methodologically sound plan for THIS question; the plan should either re-scope the research question to what the verified data can support (e.g. task-condition or purely descriptive network dynamics) as the primary outcome, or explicitly designate the halt-and-report-gap path as the expected primary result so downstream stages plan for it.

concerns.text: The 'deterministic 100-ROI contiguous-vertex scheme' parcels the fsLR surface into arbitrary contiguous vertex blocks. These are not neuroanatomically or functionally meaningful units, so the resulting 'global efficiency, modularity, participation coefficient' do not measure properties of brain networks — they measure properties of an arbitrary grouping. This is a construct-validity failure for the network-metric layer independent of the missing behavioral data. At minimum the plan must state this limitation explicitly wherever metrics are interpreted, and avoid any brain-network interpretation of the results; better, restrict claims to 'vertex-block connectivity descriptors'.

The permutation test is described as '1000 permutations of the skill proxy → null distribution of the coefficient' but does not state how covariates are handled under permutation (e.g. Freedman–Lane residual permutation vs. naive permutation of the raw proxy). With covariates in the OLS, naive permutation can yield invalid p-values. Specify the permutation scheme.

Power analysis uses TTestIndPower (two-group test) while the primary analysis is a continuous-skill OLS regression; the effect-size framework (Cohen's d) does not map to the regression coefficient being tested. Use a power analysis appropriate to the actual test (e.g. F-test / correlation power) or justify the mapping.
